description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-16) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 2 of
t/op/tie_fetch_count.t.  PRE-EXISTING (probed on a `git archive 2ac855aa`
extraction and on HEAD).  The ZERO-FETCH half of #1813's family, and a worse
bug than the double read it sits beside: this one puts the tie PROXY OBJECT
into the program's data.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s473t6a/probes/fetch4.pl):

  my $count = 0; my $stores = 0;
  sub TIESCALAR { my $pack = shift; bless [@_], $pack }
  sub FETCH  { $count++;  ${$_[0]}[0] }
  sub STORE  { $stores++; ${$_[0]}[0] = $_[1] }
  my @dummy;
  tie my $var => 'main', "abc";
  @dummy = ($var);
  print "after list assign: fetch=$count store=$stores elem=$dummy[0]\n";
  $count = 0; $stores = 0;
  $dummy[0] = "ZZZ";
  print "after elem write: fetch=$count store=$stores var=$var\n";

  perl 5.40.3: after list assign: fetch=1 store=0 elem=abc
               after elem write:  fetch=0 store=0 var=abc
  PCL        : after list assign: fetch=0 store=0 elem=#<p-tie-proxy {120198F4A3}>
               after elem write:  fetch=0 store=1 var=ZZZ

Two separate wrongs in one:
 (a) the element holds the PROXY, so printing it emits SBCL's print form into
     the program's output (the same class as #1446);
 (b) the element ALIASES the tied variable -- a write through `$dummy[0]`
     STOREs into `$var`, where perl's list assignment COPIED a value.

MECHANISM: `%p-array-store-scalar` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) walks the box's kinds
and falls through to `(t (%p-vpush (make-p-box inner) arr))` with `inner` = the
p-tie-proxy.  `%p-storable-raw` correctly declines it (a proxy is not a plain
scalar), so the raw-element gate is not involved.  Its docstring lists "a magic
cell, a tie proxy" among the kinds that "carry identity on the CONTAINER" --
true for a LIVE cell, but a COPY must read the value first.

FIX SHAPE (not taken here -- the round's budget was the double-read half):
an arm before the fall-through in `%p-array-store-scalar` and in
`%p-make-hash-entry` (the hash twin) for `(or (p-tie-proxy-p inner)
(p-magic-cell-p inner))` that stores `(make-p-box (unbox item))` instead.
PROBE THE BREAKING CASE FIRST: `@a = ($!)` and `@a = ($0)` are magic cells and
must copy their VALUES; `push @a, $tied` / `unshift` / `splice` / `p-array-init`
all append through the same helper, so the whole construction arm moves at once
(docs/boxed-aggregates-design-s455.md 4.1).  Measure the hot path: the arm sits
behind eight type tests already, so it is in the COLD part of the walk.

ROWS: t/op/tie_fetch_count.t row 14 (`@dummy = ($var) x 1`, "FETCH called just
once using 'x'").  A THIRD zero-FETCH shape is row 58, `$dummy = <$var0>` with
`$var0` tied to a glob -- readline never reads the tied scalar at all (perl 1,
PCL 0); that one is the readline operand path, not the copy path.


TWO MORE SHAPES OF THE SAME ZERO-FETCH FAMILY, found by Fable's s488 merge-review probes (scratchpad probes/p-tieref.pl + the first p1813 probe; identical on main 5eb87b01 and on the t6a tree):
 (1) A tied scalar RETURNED FROM A SUB reaches the caller as the RAW PROXY -- `sub byref { my $p = shift; $$p }  my $v = byref(\$x)` and `sub byalias { $_[0] }  my $v = byalias($x)` both print `#<p-tie-proxy {...}>` with ZERO FETCHes (perl: the value, one FETCH).  The `my $v = CALL` binding takes the `:str` raw-slot path `(%pcl-to-string-strict (p-scalar-ctx (pl-byref ...)) "$v")`, and `%pcl-to-string-strict` has no proxy arm (a rule-12 value-flows-onward silent wrong: the proxy's print-object goes into the program's output).  The top-level `$$r` / `${$r}+1` / `"$$r"` / `$r->$*` shapes FETCH correctly (deref: fetches=1), so the hole is the sub-return + raw-coercion path, not the deref.  Also `-${$_[0]}` inside a sub answers 0 with zero FETCHes (the deref yields the proxy and `%p-neg` numifies it).
 (2) LIST REPETITION copies the proxy: `my @l = ($x) x 2` -> fetches=0 (perl 2), and the elements ALIAS the tie -- the aggregate-copy shape this task already names, reached through `x`.
Fix shape for (1): the raw-slot coercions (`%pcl-to-string-strict`, `%to-number-raw`, the `:num`/`:str` binders) must go through the same proxy-aware read `unbox` uses -- ONE reading (rule 11); or the sub-return protocol (#964) FETCHes before returning a tied scalar's value, which is what perl's copy does.  Probe both vs perl before choosing; the first is the smaller diff, the second is perl's model.
subject: A tied scalar COPIED into an aggregate stores the tie PROXY: @a = ($tied) does not FETCH, prints #<p-tie-proxy> and makes the element alias the tied variable
